The different colors represent different error rates. See, when images are digitized, they are compressed. When images/pixels are compressed, it causes errors. If an image is all black, that means you don't really have any errors in the compression.

In this case, you can clearly see all the outlines of all the shapes in the image - the vehicles, the ships, etc. These white outlines are where someone went in and photoshopped the edges to smooth out the pixels. This basically means that these images have very likely been added into the image.

To be absolutely certain about the authenticity of that image, we'd need to see the original, raw, untouched image, which this is CLEARLY not. But you'll notice that the copyright at the bottom of the image also appears white in the ELA rendering, which indicates it's been added on top of the original image.

The other images are much more obviously fake, such as the one where there are two images side by side. You can pretty clearly see that the triangle shape has been added.
